items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The pianist with the Tremble Kids Orchestra was a young Swedish fellow named Ola Ringstrom

ctx.x: Not long after we moved in, I was engaged by a piano company of Zurich, Switzerland, named Jeklin, to do a tour of Switzerland, Austria and Germany with the Tremble Kids Orchestra whom I had recorded with in November 1957 in Zurich for Pathe-Marconi. Albert Nicholas and Joe Turner the pianist who was living in Switzerland, were also engaged for this tour and it was a real happy swinging deal.

I left Paris for Zurich the 27th of February rehearsed with the orchestra the 28th and we did our first date the first of March in Lugano, in the Italian part of Switzerland. Other places we played in Switzerland were Bellinzona, Ascona, Grenchen, Winterthur, Basel, Luzern, Schaffausen, Bern and Uster. The pianist with the Tremble Kids Orchestra was a young Swedish fellow named Ola Ringstrom who had a good swinging style.

The leader of the band was a clarinetist named Verner Keller. A good and lively musician. The trumpet man was named Oscar Klein and he also played guitar. Oscar was a real solid dixieland trumpeter and his style reminded me very much of Wild Bill Davison. I never knew Oscar's nationality but I think he was from Austria. Rolf Eizmek was the bass man and Charlie Antolini was the drummer and he could swing. I give the reader of this book the privilege of choosing whatever nationality they may think these last two…
